description: VLM plant symptom analysis evaluation scenarios. Cases VLM-CASE-001 to VLM-CASE-005 use sample knowledge. Cases VLM-CASE-006 to VLM-CASE-033 are a photographed Peace lily series with visual expected answers.

cases.description: Monstera with widespread lower leaf yellowing — overwatering symptom

probe_context.question: Does the Monstera show signs of widespread yellowing of lower leaves?
probe_context.worse_looks_like: Multiple older, lower leaves located nearest to the potting soil turn a solid, bright yellow color simultaneously.
probe_context.better_looks_like: The lower, older leaves of a healthy Monstera maintain the exact same deep green color as the upper canopy foliage.

expected_response.assessment: Multiple lower leaves exhibit solid bright yellow discoloration simultaneously, characteristic of prolonged soil moisture. Upper canopy remains healthy green. Pattern is consistent with overwatering stress affecting the oldest foliage first.

actual_response.assessment: Lower leaves near the soil line show uniform yellowing, suggesting the root zone has been consistently wet. The newer growth at the top appears unaffected, indicating early-stage overwatering symptoms.

cases.description: Peace lily with severe wilting and limp leaves — water deficit

probe_context.question: Does the Peace Lily show signs of severe wilting and limp drooping leaves?
probe_context.worse_looks_like: The entire plant canopy droops significantly downward over the rim of the pot. Stems lose structural firmness.
probe_context.better_looks_like: The leaves of a well-hydrated Peace Lily stand rigidly upright, holding their dark green foliage firmly.

expected_response.assessment: The entire canopy droops significantly with stems losing structural rigidity. Leaves hang limply rather than standing outward. This is consistent with severe dehydration where the root zone has become completely dry.

actual_response.assessment: Plant shows dramatic wilting with all leaves drooping downward over the pot rim. Foliage lacks turgor pressure. The condition indicates critical water deficit throughout the root zone.

cases.description: Calathea with crispy brown leaf edges — low humidity

probe_context.question: Does the Calathea show signs of crispy brown leaf edges?
probe_context.worse_looks_like: The margins and tips of leaves turn dry, brown, and brittle with a thin yellow border separating dead tissue from healthy green interior.
probe_context.better_looks_like: Leaf margins remain entirely green, smooth, and flexible right up to the very edge of the foliage.

expected_response.assessment: Leaf margins and tips show dry, brittle browning with characteristic yellow transition zone. The interior leaf tissue remains green, indicating the damage is humidity-related rather than systemic. Pattern consistent with low ambient humidity stress.

actual_response.assessment: Brown crispy edges observed along leaf margins, particularly on older leaves. A narrow yellow band separates damaged edges from the green center. Consistent with dry air conditions typical of indoor heating.
